saints.name: Sts. Processus and Martinian
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Two Roman martyrs venerated from the earliest days and honored on the Aurelian Way…
biography: Roman tradition, recorded in their ancient acts, makes Processus and Martinian warders of the Mamertine prison, where the apostles Peter and Paul were held. Converted by their prisoners, they were baptized, it is said, in a spring that miraculously welled up in the jail, and were beheaded under Nero; the matron Lucina buried them on the Aurelian Way.

Whatever the worth of the legend, their cult is among the oldest in Rome: their names stand under 2 July in the Martyrology of St. Jerome, and by the fourth century a church had risen over their tomb at the second milestone, where Gregory the Great preached on their feast and told of healings worked there.

Pope Paschal I translated their bones to a chapel of old St. Peter's between 817 and 824, and they rest today beneath the altar dedicated to them in the south transept of the basilica — among the few martyrs of the first age whose relics the centuries have kept at the heart of the Roman Church.
saints.knownFor: Their ancient and continuous veneration in the city of Rome.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
